content.text: {"verdict":"expand","impact_summary":"Correctness fixes to hook stripping (value-equality over length-equality) and session lifecycle (resume clears ended_at, early-failure containment) harden the foundational capture layer that all roadmap stages depend on.","roadmap_alignment":"The capture→distill→retrieve→intervene loop requires trustworthy session lifecycle and hook plumbing. The `ended_at = NULL` resume fix prevents phantom-ended sessions from poisoning distill and intervene metrics (maturity stalled at 61 per v0.11.0 retro). The `stripped != session_start` fix closes a correctness gap in PDI guidance removal that could silently leave orphaned hook entries — relevant as PDI is now default-ON since v0.7.0. Both fixes align with the project's hardening-before-feature-surface pattern (v0.5.0 precedent) and the v0.9.0 retro lesson that measurement infrastructure bugs compound across releases.","tidy_suggestion":"Keep as-is — these are well-scoped structural tidies with targeted regression tests. One follow-up to consider: the `_maybe_generate_intent_summary` containment initializes `project = None` but never uses the variable after the except block; verify whether downstream code paths expect a non-None project or if this is dead-write elimination waiting to happen. The `_strip_ec_inject_hooks` value-equality fix should be documented in a brief inline comment explaining why length comparison was insufficient (nested group mutation preserves count), since the subtlety will be invisible to future readers."}
